definitions.meaning: second meaning: the official documents that prove who you are

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to press a passport or ID card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' reads as a verb to apply pressure, but here it is the noun for the newspaper trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The newspapers collectively are called the press, and official identification such as passports are called one's papers.

clue.text: Paul brewed tea in a high-rise flat

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paul made a pot of tea in his tower-block apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' pretends to be an apartment; it is level ground, raised high.
explanation.definitionFit: An area of level land at high altitude is a raised flat stretch of terrain.

clue.text: Sort of dish of cooked tripe

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind of dish made from cooked tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about food; the dish is a laboratory one, a shallow glass for growing cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow lidded laboratory plate used for growing bacterial cultures is named after Julius Petri.

indicators.note: original means first or at the origin, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of recipe

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of the fish are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook copies an original recipe while preparing a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaice is a flatfish common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an object, a duplicate made to resemble it closely.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ranted or complained bitterly
second meaning: protected with a fence of bars

explanation.surface: A person was rude yet cautious in what they said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guarded' suggests a careful manner of speaking, but it means physically fenced off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail at someone is to complain angrily; a railed area is enclosed by protective bars.

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB (able seaman), plus the S
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A man's upper-class manner looks silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Tar is an old name for a sailor, whence AB. 'Jack' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd is wildly unreasonable or laughable, which matches ridiculous as a synonym.

clue.text: One who shelves his or her responsibilities

definitions.text: One who shelves his or her responsibilities

parts.words: One who shelves his or her responsibilities
parts.note: surface reading: someone who neglects their duties
setter's reading: puts things on shelves literally, the books in their care

explanation.surface: A shirker who puts off their duties.
explanation.walkthrough: To shelve normally means to postpone; here it is the literal job of placing books on shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: This person looks after a collection of books, and putting volumes back on the shelves is literally part of the job.

clue.text: They drive to and from market; a doctor taking the deliveries

definitions.text: They drive to and from market

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by a bowler

explanation.surface: Traders go to market while a doctor is delivering babies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests births or parcels; in cricket each ball bowled is a delivery and six make an over.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle and sheep herders on foot took livestock along roads between farm and market.

clue.text: Device that should catch on, if handled properly

definitions.text: Device that should catch on, if handled properly

parts.words: Device that should catch on, if handled properly
parts.note: surface reading: an invention that will become popular if marketed well
setter's reading: literally hook onto something when thrown correctly

explanation.surface: An inventor hopes a new gadget will take off with good marketing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch on' means become popular in the surface; it means physically hook onto a ledge or ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooked tool thrown on a rope to snag a wall or ship's side is designed to latch firmly onto something.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the actors in a play
second meaning: to throw or fling out

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a business venture; really the theatre troupe and a verb for throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical company is its set of performers, and to fling something outward, like a fishing line, is to throw it.

parts.note: surface reading: a modest number of foreign holidaymakers
setter's reading: a little book, carried by tourists abroad

explanation.surface: A report that few people are travelling abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' pretends to mean amount of traffic; it is a book, one pocket-sized and used by travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller's pocket guide lists useful foreign expressions for tourists visiting another country.

clue.text: Twins, for example, reversed the car

indicators.note: turned the other way round, so the preceding abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for 'for example'
the classic small British car

explanation.surface: Twin siblings backed the family car out of the drive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is the famous small British car. 'Twins' is the zodiac sign's name in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The star sign and constellation named after Castor and Pollux is known in English as the Twins.

clue.text: Shared a perfect round of golf?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: took part in, had a portion of
second, punning meaning: a round in which par was taken on every hole

explanation.walkthrough: Split as PAR TAKEN, the word describes a round played exactly to the expected score; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Having partaken of a meal or activity means having had a share in it alongside others.

parts.note: surface reading: a woman who is a reasonably justified object of criticism
setter's reading: a relative who is the target at a funfair

explanation.surface: A woman is said to be a fairly reasonable person to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is an old British fairground game: a wooden figure at which balls are thrown. 'Relatively' hints at the aunt, 'fair' at the fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground dummy pelted with sticks gave its name to anyone set up as an easy object of criticism.

parts.note: surface reading: an international summit held in the French capital
setter's reading: a French head-to-head, a summit being a head

explanation.surface: World leaders meet for talks in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase literally means head-to-head, and a summit is a top or head, so a private chat is the Parisian summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression denotes a private conversation between two people, literally one head facing another.

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of the place where they live.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British informal for rented rooms, typically a student's lodgings; to dig something is slang for liking it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the verb for enjoying something, and British usage the plural noun for a rented room.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: confine a student to college as a penalty
second meaning: the number attending a match

explanation.surface: A teacher disciplines a pupil in front of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: At British schools and colleges, to gate someone is to forbid them leaving the grounds; a football club's gate is its attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounding a pupil inside the premises is one sense; the crowd counted at a sporting fixture is the other.

parts.note: surface reading: an artist whose pictures hang in frames
setter's reading: set into window frames

explanation.surface: An artist whose work is regularly hung on walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framed' points to paintings; the work is panes of glass fitted into window frames.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who cuts and fits panes of glass into windows and doors does this job.

parts.note: surface reading: a soldier of the lowest rank in the French army
setter's reading: a French phrase meaning 'in confidence'

explanation.surface: A low-ranking soldier in the French army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' wants to be the military rank; it is the sense of confidential, expressed in a French phrase borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The borrowed phrase literally means 'between us', used to mark a remark as confidential.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... Version, an 1880s English translation

explanation.surface: An edited text of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The Revised Version was the late-Victorian update of the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrected text has been amended, and the famous Victorian scriptural translation bears this adjective in its title.

clue.text: Part of one's goal at university? Correct!

parts.note: in British usage a student is up at university
a synonym

explanation.surface: A student asks whether reaching university is part of their ambition, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' reads as an ambition; it is the goalposts of a football or rugby goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Each vertical post of a goal frame is called an upright, standing at either side.

clue.text: This by itself is only a gradual process

definitions.text: This by itself is only a gradual process

parts.note: surface reading: this thing alone
setter's reading: the word placed either side of 'by', i.e. word by word repeated

explanation.surface: A remark that something on its own makes only slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the word either side of 'by' and you get a phrase meaning step by step, gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase formed by repeating the small word around 'by' means bit by bit, gradually over time.

parts.note: surface reading: a formal leave-taking, as at a farewell ceremony
setter's reading: departure from life, by ritual suicide

explanation.surface: A formal Japanese farewell, with bows all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departure' sounds like leaving a room; it is leaving this life.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual suicide by disembowelment was the honourable death of the samurai in feudal Japan.

definitions.note: a noun for the whole building defining one room in it, fair because the vestry is part of the church and the word also names the parish's governing body

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, so the second word is placed within the first

parts.note: a synonym
a saint, abbreviated ST, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A very virtuous man is found in church.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a room in a church where clergy robe and vestments are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the room attached to a church where vestments are stored and the clergy dress for services.

clue.text: Loves an anagram to work out

indicators.note: the setter openly announces that these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzler loves working out a jumbled word.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus simply tells the solver what to do, which suits a clue about solving.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the answer to a problem or puzzle is to figure it out by reasoning.

indicators.note: settled means sorted out or arranged, so the letters of client are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A wasteful customer has finally paid off what they owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled debts' reads as paid bills, but 'settled' works on client and the debts stay as IOUs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone given to dissolute, unrestrained, immoral living and indulgence.

clue.text: Mathematical aids may finish up on the fire

definitions.meaning: first meaning: logarithms, used in calculation

definitions.text: may finish up on the fire
definitions.meaning: second meaning: chopped wood burnt in a hearth

explanation.surface: Maths tools may end up burnt, perhaps by a frustrated student.
explanation.walkthrough: The short form of logarithms, once looked up in tables for calculation, doubles as firewood.
explanation.definitionFit: Logarithm tables helped with multiplication before calculators; cut tree trunks are burnt for warmth in a grate.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: performed a reel, a lively Scottish dance
second meaning: spun dizzily, as a head swims

explanation.surface: Someone danced and then went swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swam' is not swimming but the giddy sense, as when your head swims.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a brisk Scottish dance, and staggering giddily is what a dizzy person's head feels like doing.

clue.text: The coming of the Christian faith

definitions.text: The coming of the Christian faith

parts.words: The coming of the Christian faith
parts.note: surface reading: the arrival of Christianity in a land
setter's reading: the arrival of Christ, marked as a season of the Christian year

explanation.surface: The arrival of Christianity in some new country.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a history of missionaries; the word means an arrival and names the church season before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an arrival, especially of Christ, and names the four weeks of preparation before Christmas.
